newsitem.title: UK: S&P gives BSkyB snr debt prelim BBB minus.
newsitem.headline: S&P gives BSkyB snr debt prelim BBB minus.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Monday it assigned a preliminary rating of BBB minus to BSkyB's $800 million senior debt shelf registration.
S&P said the outlook was positive.

"The rating reflects BSkyB's strong position as the UK's sole satellite direct-to-home broadcaster of pay TV entertainment and its good margins and cash flow, despite the limited track record of profitability and the narrow business base of the company," S&P said in a statement.

The rating agency said it also took into account the reinvestment requirements of the British business, the funding requirements of the recently launched German pay TV venture DF1, and expectations regarding future dividend payouts.
S&P said BSkyB continues to enjoy above average growth due largely to the popularity of its sports and movie programming.

"BSkyB is expected to continue aggressively acquiring high profile programming rights," said S&P. "Rising programming costs could restrain the operating cash flow margin, though probably not much from the healthy 31 percent level posted for fiscal 1996."

The agency said consideration of an upgrade for the rating will be linked to successful digital conversion in Britain, and to S&P becoming more comfortable with the prospects and funding needs of the German pay TV business.
